content.value_statement: Backend teams need secure implementations that prevent common vulnerabilities. This skill guides validation, authentication, API hardening, database protection, and security reviews.
actual_capabilities: Designs allowlist input validation and output encoding approaches for backend services.
Reviews API endpoints for injection, CSRF, SSRF, and unsafe error handling risks.
Guides authentication, session, JWT, OAuth, and authorization control implementation.
Recommends secure headers, cookie settings, CORS policies, and rate limiting controls.
Provides database security guidance for parameterized queries, access control, and secret handling.
Plans security logging, audit trails, and monitoring signals for backend applications.
limitations: Requires framework, language, data flow, and threat model details for precise guidance.
Cannot verify runtime behavior without access to the application, tests, and deployment configuration.
Does not replace penetration testing, compliance review, or production security monitoring.
May need adaptation for organization-specific policies, libraries, and regulatory requirements.

use_cases.title: Secure a New API Endpoint
use_cases.description: Get validation, authorization, rate limiting, and error handling guidance before implementation.

use_cases.title: Harden Authentication Flows
use_cases.description: Improve session handling, JWT use, password storage, refresh tokens, and multi-factor authentication controls.

use_cases.title: Fix Review Findings
use_cases.description: Convert security review results into focused backend code changes and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Endpoint Security
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one backend route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend endpoint for input validation, authentication, authorization, and error handling issues. Provide prioritized fixes and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure authentication flow for this application. Include password storage, sessions or tokens, refresh handling, logout, and abuse prevention.

prompt_templates.title: Harden API and Database Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a service boundary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API and database access design. Identify injection risks, authorization gaps, secret exposure, logging issues, and safe implementation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Backend Security Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across a backend system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a backend security implementation plan for this service. Cover threat assumptions, controls, tests, monitoring, rollout risks, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a login endpoint that accepts email and password.
output_examples.output: A prioritized security review covering validation, password verification, session creation, lockout behavior, error messages, logging, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Plan protection for an API that calls external URLs.
output_examples.output: An SSRF prevention plan with destination allowlists, protocol restrictions, timeouts, response limits, DNS handling, and monitoring recommendations.

output_examples.input: Fix database query risks in a reporting endpoint.
output_examples.output: A remediation checklist for parameterized queries, role-scoped access, pagination limits, audit logging, and regression tests.

best_practices: Provide the target language, framework, authentication model, and data sensitivity before asking for guidance.
Ask for verification steps and security tests with every implementation recommendation.
Review generated changes against local policies, dependency versions, and deployment configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad security advice without code, architecture context, or threat assumptions.
Do not treat generated guidance as a final compliance or penetration test result.
Do not ignore framework-specific security defaults when applying general recommendations.

faq.question: What does this skill help secure?
faq.answer: It helps secure backend code, APIs, authentication flows, database access, external requests, logging, and error handling.

faq.question: Can it write secure backend code?
faq.answer: It can provide implementation guidance and code-oriented recommendations when you supply framework and application context.

faq.question: Does it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It supports secure implementation and focused reviews, but independent security testing is still required.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the backend framework, relevant code, authentication model, data sensitivity, deployment constraints, and known risks.

faq.question: Can it help with OWASP Top 10 risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common backend risks such as injection, broken access control, SSRF, CSRF, and insecure configuration.
